findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so the conditional never applies
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers only honours conditional inclusion methods named `include_<attr>?`. The method is defined as `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never invoked and `website_name` is unconditionally serialized. Consequences: the key is emitted (with a `null` value) even when the user has no website, and, more importantly, the intended "only when a website exists" gate is dead code. Rename to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: website_name bypasses the untrusted_attributes restriction and leaks TL0 websites to anonymous users
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), so for a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor it is withheld (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`). The new `website_name` attribute derives directly from `object.user_profile.website` but has no such guard (and its `include_website_name` helper is misnamed, see other finding), so the host — and the full path when the domain matches the instance domain — is serialized to anonymous visitors for restricted users. This re-opens the spam/privacy hole that hiding `website` was meant to close. Add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (or return nil when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`).

findings.title: untrusted attribute spec not updated for website_name
findings.body: The "with a TL0 user seen as anonymous" context asserts that bio/location/website etc. are absent, but `website_name` was not added to `untrusted_attributes`. Because the new attribute is derived from the website and is currently serialized unconditionally, this spec passes while the website information still leaks. Add `website_name` to the list so the regression is caught.

findings.title: `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal and will raise under frozen_string_literal
findings.body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses the destructive `<<` on a literal receiver. It works today only because the literal is re-allocated on each evaluation; if `# frozen_string_literal: true` is ever added to this file (common in this codebase) it raises `FrozenError` on every profile serialization. Use non-mutating concatenation, e.g. `".#{website_host}"`.

findings.title: Hostname comparison is case-sensitive and path-only (query/fragment dropped, bare `/` shown)
findings.body: `URI(...).host` preserves the case the user typed, so a profile website of `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` will not match `Discourse.current_hostname` (`example.com`) and the full path will not be shown; comparisons should downcase both hosts. Additionally `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` yields a trailing `example.com/` for root URLs and silently drops any query string, so the displayed text can differ from the actual link target.

findings.title: Websites stored without a scheme now render no label at all
findings.body: `URI('example.com/user').host` is nil, so `website_name` returns nil and the template's `{{#if model.website_name}}` hides the link entirely. The previous client-side implementation (`website.split('/')[2]`) also mis-handled such values, but it at least produced a truthy string in some cases; now a stored scheme-less website makes the globe/link disappear from the profile. Consider falling back to the raw website string (or normalizing by prefixing `http://`) when no host can be parsed.
